## Gurobi and HiGHS: attained quality and computational effort

The completed h215 W STO calculations use the same frozen workbook,
ordered warehouses, selected directed network, nine equiprobable scenarios
and scalar coefficients. Both Pyomo pipelines use the bounded candidate-slack
representation of Appendix C. This gives a more specific comparison basis
than the h215 label alone. The earlier HiGHS record has no ordered-algebra
fingerprint; its retained input bindings, model dimensions and bound policy
agree with the common formulation, but an unrecorded fingerprint is not
inferred retrospectively.

| Setting | Gurobi / APPSI | HiGHS / APPSI |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Native version | 13.0.3 | 1.15.1 |
| Pyomo version | 6.10.1 | 6.10.1 |
| Native time allowance, s | 28,800 | 28,800 |
| Relative MIP gap target | 0.01 | 0.01 |
| Thread ceiling | 4 | 4 |
| Seed setting | Seed = 42 | random_seed = 42 |
| Feasibility controls | FeasibilityTol and IntFeasTol = 1e-9 | mip_feasibility_tolerance = 1e-9 |

: Effective configurations of the completed Pyomo h215 W STO observations.
The historical HiGHS log records parallel tree search off; this differs from
the ongoing parallel-search campaign. {#tbl-pyomo-settings}

The Gurobi calculation supplied an ordered pre-solve algebra fingerprint
for 14,054,654 variables, 307 binaries, 735,577 linear constraints and
52,217,866 nonzeros. The earlier HiGHS model has the same dimensions.
Matching dimensions alone do not prove identical coefficients or identical
native presolved models. Original input and mathematical-contract checks
therefore accompany the dimensional comparison.

Both returned incumbents passed their original independent primal
validation and the prescribed 1% scalar-gap criterion.

| Implementation | Objective, BRL trillion | Common gap, % | Native runtime, min |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Pyomo/APPSI Gurobi | 13.071397 | 0.740159 | 31.54 |
| Pyomo/APPSI HiGHS | 12.974673 | 0.000196 | 426.70 |

: Attained scalar quality and native computation time for the two completed
Pyomo observations. These are separate single runs, not matched repeated
measurements at equal attained gaps. {#tbl-highs-h215}

| Implementation | Application end-to-end, min | Sampled worker-tree peak, GiB |
|:--|--:|--:|
| Pyomo/APPSI Gurobi | 55.621 | 55.390 |
| Pyomo/APPSI HiGHS | 441.202 | 55.218 |

: Observed application time and sampled process-tree memory. Sampling can miss
an instantaneous peak; these values are distinct from requested memory and
native solver-managed memory. {#tbl-pyomo-outcomes}

Gurobi's lower bound was 12.974647770397 trillion BRL; the HiGHS lower bound
was 12.974647770397 trillion BRL at the shown precision. HiGHS's smaller
incumbent is compatible with the Gurobi interval. Its much tighter attained
gap does not imply that Gurobi would need its reported runtime to attain
that same quality, or that HiGHS would need its full observed time to attain
only the 1% threshold. The comparison reports the outcomes actually
retained, rather than interpolating unobserved stopping times.

The HiGHS financial subtotal is 393.331 billion BRL, domestic service is
92.3284%, and artificial penalties account for 96.9685% of its objective.
Thus, a near-zero scalar gap coexists with substantial modeled shortages
and capacity exceedances. Objective precision, financial interpretation
and physical service answer different questions.

The HiGHS log records one processed node and 2,901,682 LP iterations.
Its four-thread ceiling coexisted with one maximum search worker and
parallel search off. These observations illustrate why a thread setting is
not itself a measure of parallel work. The native Gurobi cohort in the
preceding section uses a different implementation and original time profile;
it is not pooled with the repeated common-Pyomo campaign.

The [retained HiGHS input and validation record](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/ad2ded8132bf5171be65c0113b3d0026c22b2e7b/docs/evidence/scalar_highs_h215_2226536_inspection.json)
and the original source-bound experiment records retain the certificate
scope. Appendix E presents the corresponding accepted investment and flow
summaries. The new common-Pyomo scaling cohort is reported separately below.
